C0.quote: we conceptualize such problems in a voting scenario
C0.note: Districting (regrouping voters into districts) evaluated by plurality margin of victory per group; computational aspect of district-based voting. School application is a non-electoral mapping of the same model.

C1.quote: We show that the Fair Regrouping problem is NP-complete for
C1.note: Main results: NP-completeness (Thm 4.1, 4.4), XP algorithm (Thm 4.5), greedy heuristics evaluated on synthetic graphs (SI) and on UK 2017 election and Detroit school data (EM).

C2.2.loc: Sec 3 Preliminaries, p.1307; proof of Thm 4.4, p.1308
C2.2.quote: Each voter has a most preferred alternative whom the voter votes for
C2.2.note: OTH: input is a single most preferred alternative (plurality vote). RANK: the Thm 4.4 construction writes votes as strict orders over two alternatives (x ≻ y); synthetic data generate a preference over alternatives by distance.

C2.3.quote: each having one preferred alternative (out of m)
C2.3.note: Voters have a preferred alternative (preference) distinguished verbally from the vote cast for it.

C2.4.quote: Each voter has a most preferred alternative whom the voter votes for
C2.4.note: States that each voter votes for the most preferred alternative, without a reason. Elsewhere the rule and margin of victory are phrased directly on preferences (IDU-like), but the explicit statement takes precedence.

C5.1.note: Claims about representation of voters, minority groups and opposition parties, and about everyone's opinion being valued.

C5.2.quote: The margin of victory is the minimum number of votes that needs
C5.2.note: Representation is assessed via plurality margin of victory computed on votes, which are stated to be votes for the most preferred alternative.

VOT.quote_behav: Each voter has a most preferred alternative whom the voter votes for
VOT.note: Voters are moved between groups by the regrouping; their votes are fixed. Students in the school application 'vote' for their reported race.

CAN.loc_info: Checked: Sec 1 Introduction, Sec 3 Preliminaries, Sec 4, Sec 6 Conclusion
CAN.note: Alternatives (parties/candidates) take no action in the model; their interests are discussed informally (Sec 1, p.1306: elected candidate incentivized to engage with electorate; representation of opposition parties in Sec 6).

DIS.quote_behav: such that the maximum margin of victory of any group is minimized
DIS.quote_info: a set V of n voters along with their corresponding preferences
DIS.note: The regrouping agent (policy-makers, online platform; Sec 1 p.1306, Sec 5.2 p.1311) optimises a partition to minimise maximum margin of victory; objective is the paper's fairness objective rather than self-interest, so STRAT vs NONSTRAT was a doubt; STRAT chosen as optimiser. Knowledge of all voters' preferences follows from the problem input. Partisan gerrymanderers are discussed informally in Sec 1.
